subject: Request: Customer network attribution & latency exclusion for Private VPC deployment
messages:
From: Sanjay Rao <sanjay.rao@novumhealth.com>
To: rachel.kim@redwood.com
Cc: Maya Patel <m.patel@novumhealth.com>, legal@novumhealth.com
Date: 2028-08-15 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Private VPC: request for explicit customer-network latency carve-out

Rachel — thanks again for the demo last week. As we scope the Private VPC deployment we need to lock down the SLA language around tail latency attributable to Novum-managed network segments (on-prem edge, MPLS circuits, and our last-mile provider).

Specifically: Novum will own any latency/packet loss that originates within or is caused by our customer-managed layers. We are asking Redwood to add an explicit appendix that: 1) excludes customer network tail (defined as hops under our administrative control) from Redwood uptime/latency SLOs, and 2) lists the minimal telemetry and trace artifacts you need to validate whether an incident is customer-side.

I'll attach a sample packet capture and summary from our NOC. Please let me know what format you need and what the proposed appendix language would look like. We have procurement timelines; ideally we finalize this by EOD Aug 24.

— Sanjay
Novum Health — Head of Platform Ops
From: rachel.kim@redwood.com
To: Sanjay Rao <sanjay.rao@novumhealth.com>
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, lauren_bishop@redwood.com
Date: 2028-08-15 12:20:14 -0700
Subject: Re: Private VPC: request for explicit customer-network latency carve-out

Hi Sanjay — thanks for the note and the pcap. We can accommodate a measured carve-out for customer-controlled network boundaries, but there are a few items we need to align on so both sides have clear acceptance criteria.

High level proposed approach:
- Redwood will include a "Customer Network Attribution" appendix that documents: the exclusion scope, data artifacts required for validation, and a timeline for remediation attribution.
- Exclusion will apply only when evidence shows the fault originates in customer-administered segments (edge routers, on-prem firewalls, or transit under Novum control).
- Redwood will continue to own end-to-end service degradation when our runtime, scheduling, or model variants are implicated.

Next steps we need from Novum:
- Traces/pcaps (you've already sent one, thanks) and summary of your last-mile provider(s).
- Preferred definition of "customer-administered segment" in a short bullet list.
- Any constraints from your legal team about indemnity or acceptance windows.

Looping in Marcus (Legal) and Karthik (Solutions) to draft the appendix and the telemetry checklist. I'll pull together a single PDF with proposed text and a short runbook. Expect a draft by EOD tomorrow.

Thanks — Rachel
Rachel Kim
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
From: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>
To: rachel.kim@redwood.com, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Cc: lauren_bishop@redwood.com
Date: 2028-08-16 08:45:03 -0700
Subject: Re: Private VPC: request for explicit customer-network latency carve-out

Rachel / team — I reviewed Novum's request and drafted an initial appendix that balances Redwood's SLA obligations with customer-controlled infrastructure. Key legal points in the draft (attached as proposed-sla-carveout-appendix.pdf):

- "Customer Network Tail Exclusion": Redwood's SLOs (including 99.95% uptime and 95th/99th latency bands) shall not be deemed breached when credible evidence indicates the root cause is within Customer-Administered Network Segments.
- Evidence required: packet captures with timestamps, traceroutes showing hop ownership, BGP route announcements or peering logs if applicable, and a signed incident attribution statement from a named Novum Network Engineer within 72 hours of incident detection.
- Redwood reserves the right to validate artifacts and request additional telemetry; validation periods and dispute resolution steps are defined.
- Indemnity carve-outs are narrowly scoped; Redwood's liability remains for misconfigurations of Redwood-controlled connectors and proxies.

I flagged two negotiable items for Novum: the 72-hour acceptance window (we can extend to 120 hours for complex on-prem investigations) and whether both parties sign off on attribution statements (preferred).

Attaching draft. Marcus
Marcus Lin
Senior Counsel, Redwood Inference
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
To: rachel.kim@redwood.com, marcus_lin@redwood.com
Cc: lauren_bishop@redwood.com
Date: 2028-08-16 10:30:22 -0700
Subject: Re: Private VPC: request for explicit customer-network latency carve-out

Quick technical checklist for the runbook we should attach and send to Novum (see runbook-telemetry-checklist.docx attachment):

- Required artifacts for an attribution: synchronized timestamps (NTP), raw pcap (covering client <-> egress router <-> peering point), traceroute outputs from both sides, and metrics from the on-prem edge (interface counters, queuing stats).
- Minimum sampling: 5 minutes of full-rate pcap around incident start + 30s pre/post window; where pcaps are large, we accept summarized tcpdump with annotated timestamps plus tcpdump rotation metadata.
- Preferred metadata fields: flow hashes, connection IDs, Redwoods request IDs (if present), BGP AS path, and peering interface identifiers.
- Suggested SLO appendix language calls out that Redwood will attempt to assist in triage but will not accept full attribution without the artifacts above.

Also advise Novum on optional steps to reduce false positives: v4/v6 dual-traceroutes, synthetic heartbeat checks at 30s, and a short config checklist for edge queueing policies.

Karthik
Principal Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
From: rachel.kim@redwood.com
To: Sanjay Rao <sanjay.rao@novumhealth.com>
Cc: Maya Patel <m.patel@novumhealth.com>, legal@novumhealth.com, marcus_lin@redwood.com, karthik_iyer@redwood.com
Date: 2028-08-17 15:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Private VPC: request for explicit customer-network latency carve-out

Sanjay — thanks for the quick turnaround on the pcap. Attached is our consolidated proposal: a short SLA appendix (proposed-sla-carveout-appendix.pdf) and a technical runbook (runbook-telemetry-checklist.docx) that specifies exactly what artifacts we need to accept a customer-network attribution.

Summary of what's included:
- "Customer Network Tail Exclusion" appendix with the definition you asked for and a dispute resolution workflow.
- Evidence matrix (what you provide vs where Redwood may request additional data).
- Extended acceptance window option (we've proposed 120 hours to be flexible for on-prem investigations).

Requested action from Novum:
1) Confirm you can provide the artifact set in the runbook (pcap + traceroutes + signed engineer statement) or tell us which items you'd want to modify.
2) If the appendix language is acceptable, please confirm and we will send a DocuSign for the amendment. Link to draft in our workspace: https://docs.google.com/document/d/1a2b3c-proposed-sla-appendix

If you prefer, we can set a short call with Marcus and Karthik to walk through the appendix and the tech checklist. Otherwise, please reply with confirmation by EOD Aug 24 so we can keep procurement on schedule.

Best — Rachel
Rachel Kim
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
Attachments: proposed-sla-carveout-appendix.pdf (draft), runbook-telemetry-checklist.docx (technical), novum-network-traces-aug14.pcap (sample from Novum)
